summary: A Sydney Morning Herald markets wrap says the ASX rose after Wall Street gains driven by dovish Fed comments, falling Treasury yields and hopes of Chinese stimulus. Oil dropped after Monday's rally while investors watched the Israel–Hamas conflict. The note also covers ASX laggards such as Bank of Queensland and healthcare stocks, and upcoming US data.
one_line: ASX climbed on falling bond yields, dovish Fed remarks and China stimulus hopes, while oil eased amid Middle East conflict worries.
key_facts: Healthcare companies fell 0.1 per cent on the ASX even though CSL (down 0.4 per cent) delivered broadly in line with expectations.
Bank of Queensland shed 6.9 per cent after missing consensus expectations.

TMS Capital portfolio manager Ben Clark attributed the ASX strength to a calming bond market, a positive Wall Street lead and positive news out of China, including rumours of a substantial Chinese stimulus package.
Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic said the US central bank did not need to raise interest rates any further and that he saw no recession ahead.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.4 per cent to 33,739.30, the S&P 500 gained 0.5 per cent and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.6 per cent.
The 10-year Treasury yield came off its 16-year peak, tumbling as much as 18 basis points to 4.62 per cent, on track for its steepest single-day drop since May.
West Texas Intermediate settled below $US86 a barrel following its biggest rally since April.
The Australian dollar was US64.20¢ at the close as the US dollar fell for a fifth straight day, its longest losing streak since July.
Fed swaps showed about a 60 per cent chance the Fed will stay on hold in December, compared with 60 per cent odds on another rate rise a week earlier.
Paul Tudor Jones told CNBC the geopolitical environment was the 'most threatening and challenging' he'd ever seen and predicted a US recession early next year.
Finland is on high alert as it suspects a Baltic Sea gas pipeline leak was caused by a deliberate act of destruction, and European gas prices jumped.
Investors await the September Fed meeting minutes on Wednesday, Thursday's consumer price index and Friday's University of Michigan consumer-sentiment survey.
